steps.intent: Our primary objective as penholder is to secure a 12-month extension of the Panel of Experts mandate under the 1591 sanctions regime while reinforcing demands to end the RSF siege of El Fasher and curb illicit arms and mercenary flows into Darfur. We anticipate resistance from the Russian Federation and China regarding explicit references to the RSF siege and external weapons supplies, as well as any push to expand arms embargo restrictions beyond Darfur. To prevent a veto, the text maintains targeted, agreed language from resolution 2736 (2024) and retains the standard, focused architecture of resolution 2750 (2024).

messages.Algeria: Algeria supports the renewal of the Panel of Experts' mandate to address destabilizing arms flows, foreign recruitment, and external interference fueling the tragic conflict in Darfur. However, the text must fully respect Sudan's sovereignty and avoid placing the legitimate state authorities on an equal footing with non-state armed actors, notably by explicitly acknowledging the Government of Sudan's sovereign decisions regarding humanitarian crossings. In line with the consistent position of the A3 on sanctions regimes, the review of benchmarks must also clearly aim toward the eventual easing and lifting of measures so as not to unduly hinder the State's capacity to protect civilians.
messages.China: China supports the renewal of the mandate of the Panel of Experts to assist the Council in monitoring the situation, but we reiterate that sanctions are merely a means, not an end. The Security Council must establish a clear and realistic path toward adjusting and lifting sanctions on Darfur through regular review of the benchmarks. Furthermore, the Panel must execute its mandate with strict impartiality and objectivity, maintaining constructive engagement with the sovereign Government of the Sudan.
messages.Denmark: Denmark strongly supports the timely renewal of the mandate of the Panel of Experts, whose independent monitoring remains indispensable given the catastrophic situation and ongoing violations in Darfur. We urge the penholder to explicitly condemn conflict-related sexual violence and attacks on humanitarian workers in the preambular text, reflecting the horrific realities on the ground. We also propose correcting the reporting sequence in OP2 so that the Panel's final report logically follows its interim report ahead of the mandate's expiration.
messages.France: France strongly supports the draft resolution and commends the United States for circulating a text that ensures the continuity of the Panel of Experts' critical monitoring role. In light of the appalling abuses documented on the ground, we believe it is essential to explicitly condemn conflict-related sexual violence. We also note a minor chronological adjustment required in operative paragraph 2 regarding the final reporting deadline.
messages.Greece: Greece strongly supports the renewal of the mandate of the 1591 Panel of Experts, whose independent monitoring is essential given the alarming escalation in Darfur and persistent arms embargo violations. We ask the penholder to explicitly condemn conflict-related sexual and gender-based violence, which continues to be deployed as a horrific weapon of war in Sudan. In addition, we suggest adjusting the date of the final report in operative paragraph 2 to ensure a logical chronological sequence following the interim report.
messages.Guyana: Guyana reaffirms its steadfast support for the vital work of the Panel of Experts and welcomes the draft extending its mandate. In line with the A3+ priorities, we emphasize the urgent need to stem foreign interference and the external supply of arms and mercenaries that continue to fuel atrocities in Darfur and across the Sudan. We look forward to working constructively with the penholder and all Council members to achieve a unified text.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports the technical rollover and renewal of the Panel of Experts' mandate to monitor the situation in Darfur. However, sanctions regimes must not remain indefinite and must be regularly reviewed against realistic benchmarks, respecting the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Sudan. We also urge the penholder to correct the reporting timeline in paragraph 2 and ensure that the Panel conducts its work in full consultation with the host government.
messages.Panama: Panama commends the United States for preparing this draft and strongly supports the timely extension of the Panel of Experts' mandate, whose independent reporting is indispensable for monitoring the arms embargo and documenting violations of international humanitarian law. Given the grave patterns of abuse documented across Darfur, we propose including an explicit reference to conflict-related sexual violence to ensure the Council reflects the full scope of civilian suffering and the imperative of accountability. Panama stands ready to support the adoption of this resolution.
messages.Republic of Korea: As Chair of the 1591 Sanctions Committee, the Republic of Korea strongly supports the extension of the mandate of the Panel of Experts and thanks the United States for preparing this draft. We wish to flag a technical correction in OP2 to ensure the Panel's reporting schedule is chronologically aligned with the September 2026 mandate extension, with the interim report preceding the final report. We also encourage reflecting the critical need to address and monitor conflict-related sexual violence given the grave humanitarian and human rights situation on the ground.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation supports the extension of the mandate of the Panel of Experts, but insists on full respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Sudan and the primary role of its legitimate government. Council sanctions imposed two decades ago under completely different realities cannot remain indefinite punitive instruments, and the Council must commit to clear prospects for lifting them in light of established benchmarks. Furthermore, any humanitarian initiatives, including border crossings, must fully respect the sovereign authority of Port Sudan and UN Guiding Principles.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone strongly supports the extension of the mandate of the Panel of Experts and the enforcement of the targeted sanctions and arms embargo to stem the catastrophic violence in Darfur. Informed by our own history, we attach the utmost priority to the protection of civilians, particularly women and children who bear the brunt of atrocities and sexual violence. We also emphasize the central role of African-led mediation through the African Union and IGAD in achieving an immediate, permanent ceasefire and sustainable peace in the Sudan.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia fully supports the swift renewal of the mandate of the Panel of Experts, whose independent monitoring of the Darfur arms embargo and human rights violations remains indispensable. We urge the penholder to reflect the Council's deep concern over the appalling levels of conflict-related sexual violence and ethnically motivated attacks against civilians, especially women and children. We also propose a technical alignment in paragraph 2 to ensure the final report follows the interim report in proper chronological sequence.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the extension of the Panel of Experts' mandate and commends the penholder's efforts to address the alarming security and humanitarian crisis in Darfur. However, it is vital that the resolution unequivocally reaffirms the sovereignty and primary responsibility of the Sudanese State, while establishing a clear perspective on the review and progressive lifting of sanctions in accordance with the established benchmarks. We also urge stronger language against external interference that continues to undermine Sudan's national stability and regional security.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom strongly supports the draft resolution and thanks the United States for circulating a timely and robust text renewing the vital mandate of the 1591 Panel of Experts. We propose reflecting the Council's grave concern regarding rampant conflict-related sexual violence in Darfur and adjusting the reporting timeline in OP2 to ensure the final report follows the interim report. We look forward to working closely with the penholder and Council members to secure the swift adoption of this text.

With this technical adjustment, China is prepared to support the draft resolution.
messages.Denmark: Denmark thanks the United States for accommodating our proposals to strengthen language on conflict-related sexual and gender-based violence, grave violations against children, and the protection of humanitarian and medical personnel, as well as fixing the reporting schedule. The draft resolution is well-balanced, reinforces the integrity of the 1591 sanctions regime, and ensures the Panel of Experts can continue its vital independent monitoring work. Denmark fully supports the current text and is ready to vote in favour.
messages.France: France thanks the United States for incorporating our proposals into revision 1, particularly on conflict-related sexual and gender-based violence and the reporting timeline. The independent monitoring work of the Panel of Experts remains indispensable given the catastrophic escalation in Darfur and widespread violations of the arms embargo. France fully supports the adoption of this draft resolution without delay.
messages.Greece: Greece thanks the United States for incorporating our proposals into Revision 1, particularly on addressing conflict-related sexual violence and reporting timelines. We fully support the renewal of the Panel of Experts' mandate as a vital tool for monitoring the arms embargo and human rights violations. Greece is prepared to vote in favour of the text as currently drafted.
messages.Guyana: Guyana commends the United States for its constructive engagement and for incorporating our key priorities into Revision 1, notably regarding external interference, the illicit flow of weapons, the recruitment of foreign fighters, and the protection of civilians and children. The revised text provides a balanced and robust basis for extending the vital mandate of the Panel of Experts. Guyana is pleased to support the draft resolution as currently formulated and looks forward to voting in favour.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan appreciates the penholder's constructive approach in incorporating our proposals regarding the reporting timeline, benchmark reviews, and engagement with the host government. We maintain that sanctions and expert panels operate most effectively when conducted in close consultation with the sovereign authorities of the Sudan and oriented towards clear, realistic benchmarks. With this minor refinement in paragraph 4, Pakistan is fully prepared to support the draft resolution.
messages.Panama: Panama thanks the United States for incorporating our language on conflict-related sexual and gender-based violence into the draft text. We fully support the renewal of the Panel of Experts' mandate as an indispensable tool for monitoring compliance with the sanctions regime and protecting civilians in Darfur. Panama finds the current text balanced and comprehensive, and we stand ready to vote in favor.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea thanks the United States for accommodating our proposals in the revised draft, particularly regarding the realistic reporting timeline for the Panel of Experts and the explicit condemnation of conflict-related sexual violence. We fully support the adoption of this draft resolution as currently drafted.
messages.Russian Federation: We appreciate the penholder's constructive efforts to accommodate our concerns in Revision 1, particularly regarding the review of benchmarks and acknowledging the decision of the Sudanese authorities on the Adre crossing. To finalize consensus on the text, it is essential to reflect that humanitarian assistance must adhere to the UN guiding principles, including respect for the sovereignty and primary role of the host State. With this targeted adjustment, the Russian Federation will be in a position to vote in favour of the draft resolution.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone thanks the penholder for constructively incorporating our proposed amendments into Revision 1, particularly regarding conflict-related sexual violence, grave violations against children, and the pivotal mediation role of the African Union and IGAD. The revised draft strikes an appropriate balance, reaffirming Sudan's sovereignty while reinforcing the protection of civilians and the crucial monitoring mandate of the Panel of Experts. Sierra Leone fully supports the text as currently drafted and stands ready to vote in favour.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia thanks the United States for accommodating our priorities regarding conflict-related sexual violence, the protection of children, and reporting timelines in revision 1. The draft provides a robust and balanced framework that ensures the uninterrupted and vital monitoring work of the Panel of Experts in Darfur. We fully support this text and look forward to its swift adoption.
messages.Somalia: Somalia appreciates the penholder's constructive efforts to accommodate our concerns in Revision 1, particularly on curbing external interference, addressing the illicit flow of arms and mercenaries, and reaffirming the responsibility of Sudanese authorities to protect civilians. We are ready to support this draft and encourage the inclusion of close consultations with the Government of the Sudan when reviewing benchmarks for adjusting or lifting sanctions. We urge all Council members to support this balanced text to assist regional and international efforts in restoring peace to the Sudan.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom strongly supports the draft resolution renewing the mandate of the Panel of Experts on the Sudan until September 2026. We thank the United States for incorporating our proposals, particularly on condemning conflict-related sexual violence and establishing an effective reporting timeline for the Panel. The Panel's independent reporting remains vital to monitoring compliance with the Darfur arms embargo and documenting external interference, and we look forward to the swift adoption of this text.

before.United States of America:
Thank you, Madam President. 

The United States has put forward this draft resolution to extend the mandate of the Panel of Experts assisting the 1591 Sudan Sanctions Committee for an additional twelve months. 

The catastrophic situation in Sudan, and particularly in Darfur, demands our urgent attention and unity. As the Rapid Support Forces continue their brutal siege and assault on El Fasher, and as fighting spreads devastating violence, sexual violence, and famine across Sudan, the work of the Panel of Experts is more indispensable than ever. Their independent monitoring and reporting provide this Council and the international community with critical, unvarnished facts regarding violations of international humanitarian law and the illicit flow of weapons into Darfur.

The arms embargo on Darfur remains a vital tool to stem the weapons and materiel fueling atrocities against civilians. This draft resolution reflects extensive consultations, underscores the primary responsibility to protect civilians, addresses the urgent need for unhindered humanitarian access, and calls on all external actors to cease fueling this devastating war. 

We urge all members of the Security Council to vote in favour of this draft resolution and send a clear, unified message in support of peace, accountability, and the people of Sudan. Thank you.

after.Algeria:
Madam President,

Algeria voted in favour of the resolution just adopted, which extends the mandate of the Panel of Experts assisting the 1591 Sanctions Committee for an additional year. We thank the United States, as penholder, for its efforts throughout the negotiation process to maintain Council unity on this critical text.

Our affirmative vote reflects our steadfast commitment to supporting all international efforts aimed at bringing an end to the tragic conflict that continues to bring untold suffering upon the brotherly people of the Sudan, particularly in Darfur. 

As we witness the catastrophic humanitarian situation, the ongoing siege and military escalation in and around El Fasher, and the persistent attacks against civilians and camps for internally displaced persons, the protection of civilians must remain our utmost priority. In this regard, we welcome the sovereign and commendable decision of the Government of the Sudan to extend the opening of the Adre border crossing, which is vital to facilitating the rapid, safe, and unhindered delivery of life-saving humanitarian assistance.

Algeria firmly reiterates that any action taken by this Council must strictly adhere to the fundamental principles of full respect for the sovereignty, independence, unity, and territorial integrity of the Sudan. We reaffirm that the Sudanese state and its legitimate national institutions bear the primary responsibility for the protection of civilians and the preservation of national stability. In this context, we once again stress that the internationally recognized Government of the Sudan and the Rapid Support Forces must never be placed on an equal footing.

Furthermore, my delegation emphasizes that the arms embargo on Darfur must be strictly enforced. We remain deeply concerned by continued external interference, the illicit flow of weapons, and the recruitment and financing of foreign fighters and mercenaries, which only serve to prolong the war and deepen the suffering of the Sudanese people. Such destabilizing external interference must cease immediately.

Finally, Algeria has consistently maintained that United Nations sanctions regimes are not ends in themselves and must never be punitive or perpetual. They must remain adaptive to developments on the ground. We therefore welcome the Council’s commitment in paragraph 7 of the resolution to review the benchmarks in close consultation with the Government of the Sudan, with a clear view toward the adjustment, suspension, or progressive lifting of these measures.

Algeria will continue to stand in full solidarity with the Sudan and its people, and we reiterate our support for African-led and regional mediation efforts, led by the African Union and IGAD, to achieve an immediate, comprehensive ceasefire and a peaceful, Sudanese-owned political solution.

I thank you.
after.China:
Madam President,

China voted in favour of the resolution just adopted extending the mandate of the Panel of Experts assisting the 1591 Committee. 

The ongoing conflict in the Sudan has caused severe civilian casualties and a deteriorating humanitarian situation. China is deeply saddened by the suffering of the Sudanese people. We call on all parties to the conflict to put the interests of the country and its people first, immediately cease hostilities, de-escalate the situation, earnestly protect civilians and civilian infrastructure in accordance with international humanitarian law, and resolve differences through dialogue and political negotiations. We welcome the decision of the Sudanese Government to extend the opening of the Adre border crossing, which facilitates the delivery of humanitarian assistance to people in need.

I wish to emphasize the following points regarding the resolution and the work of the Panel of Experts:

First, the sovereignty, independence, unity, and territorial integrity of the Sudan must be earnestly respected. The Sudanese Government bears the primary responsibility for protecting civilians and maintaining national peace and stability. The international community and the Security Council should respect the ownership and leadership of the Sudanese Government and avoid imposing external solutions or exerting undue pressure. 

Second, Security Council sanctions are a means, not an end, and should never be applied indefinitely. The Council should regularly review the sanctions measures against the Sudan in light of developments on the ground and, in close consultation with the Sudanese Government, actively advance the review of relevant benchmarks with a view to adjusting, suspending, or progressively lifting the sanctions. 

Third, the Panel of Experts must strictly abide by its mandate, adhere to the principles of objectivity, impartiality, and neutrality, and base its reporting on credible, reliable, and verifiable information. It should strengthen communication and cooperation with the Sudanese Government, listen fully to its views, and play a constructive role in supporting the work of the Committee and the Council.

China will continue to work with the international community, particularly the African Union and regional organizations, to support regional mediation efforts, adhere to the principle of African solutions to African problems, and play a constructive role in restoring peace and stability in the Sudan at an early date.

Thank you, Madam President.
after.Denmark:
Madam President,

Denmark voted in favour of the resolution today, and we welcome the unanimous adoption extending the mandate of the Panel of Experts assisting the 1591 Committee. At a time of deepening tragedy across the Sudan, the Security Council’s unity today sends a necessary signal of our collective commitment to peace, accountability, and the protection of civilians.

The situation in Darfur, and particularly in and around El Fasher, remains catastrophic. Civilians are enduring relentless shelling, acute food insecurity, horrific levels of conflict-related sexual and gender-based violence, and deliberate attacks on camps for internally displaced persons, including Abu Shouk. Denmark reiterates this Council’s unequivocal demand: the Rapid Support Forces must immediately halt the siege and assault on El Fasher. All parties must respect their obligations under international humanitarian law and international human rights law.

To prevent further atrocities, curbing the flow of weapons into Darfur is essential. The Panel of Experts plays an indispensable role through its independent, objective, and evidence-based reporting on violations of the arms embargo and international humanitarian law. We call on all parties and Member States to fully cooperate with the Panel and ensure its unhindered access. 

Furthermore, we urge all Member States to strictly comply with the arms embargo and refrain from external interference, including the supply of weapons, military material, and foreign fighters, which only fuels this devastating war.

Finally, we emphasize the urgent need for safe, rapid, and unhindered humanitarian access across all borders and conflict lines to reach millions on the brink of famine. We welcome the decision to maintain the opening of the Adre border crossing and stress that humanitarians and medical personnel must be protected.

The people of the Sudan have suffered unimaginable horrors for far too long. Denmark remains steadfast in its support for an immediate cessation of hostilities, an inclusive political process, and full accountability for all violations and abuses committed throughout this conflict.

Thank you.
after.France:
Madam President,

France welcomes the unanimous adoption of the resolution extending the mandate of the Panel of Experts assisting the 1591 Committee for an additional year.

This unanimity sends an essential signal of unity from the Security Council at a time when the crisis in the Sudan is reaching unprecedented, catastrophic proportions. The independent and impartial reporting of the Panel of Experts remains indispensable to shedding light on the grave violations of international humanitarian law and human rights, as well as to monitoring compliance with the arms embargo in Darfur.

The situation on the ground is horrific. We condemn in the strongest terms the continued siege and relentless assaults against El Fasher and displacement camps such as Abu Shouk by the Rapid Support Forces, as well as indiscriminate strikes and clashes that continue to claim countless civilian lives. We remain deeply alarmed by widespread sexual and gender-based violence, violations against children, and the acute famine devastating millions of Sudanese.

France calls on all parties to immediately cease hostilities and commit to a permanent ceasefire. In accordance with resolution 2736 (2024), the RSF must immediately halt its siege of El Fasher. 

We reiterate that the arms embargo on Darfur must be strictly respected by all Member States. The continued influx of weapons and foreign fighters only fuels the cycle of violence and deepens the suffering of the civilian population. All external interference must end immediately.

Finally, we recall that all parties have the obligation under international humanitarian law to protect civilians and civilian infrastructure, and to allow and facilitate rapid, safe, and unhindered humanitarian access. In this regard, we welcome the decision to maintain the opening of the Adre crossing from Chad and urge that all humanitarian corridors remain fully open and functional.

France will continue to stand resolutely alongside the Sudanese people and remains fully committed to supporting regional and international mediation efforts, including those of the African Union and the Personal Envoy of the Secretary-General, to achieve a peaceful, inclusive, and lasting political solution.

I thank you.
after.Greece:
Thank you, Madam President.

Greece voted in favour of the resolution just adopted, extending the mandate of the Panel of Experts assisting the 1591 Sanctions Committee for another year. We welcome the Council's unanimous adoption today, which demonstrates our collective commitment to addressing the catastrophic crisis in Sudan.

The situation across Sudan, and particularly in Darfur, remains deeply alarming. The ongoing siege and relentless military escalation in and around El Fasher, along with repeated attacks against civilians, displacement camps such as Abu Shouk, and critical civilian infrastructure, have inflicted unimaginable suffering on millions of innocent people. We are particularly horrified by the widespread reports of conflict-related sexual and gender-based violence, violations against children, and attacks on healthcare and humanitarian personnel. 

Greece reiterates its call for an immediate and permanent cessation of hostilities, the lifting of the siege of El Fasher in accordance with resolution 2736 (2024), and full compliance by all parties with their obligations under international humanitarian law and international human rights law. The protection of civilians and the facilitation of rapid, safe, and unhindered humanitarian access to all those in need remain paramount. In this regard, we welcome the decision to keep the Adre border crossing open.

The targeted sanctions regime and the arms embargo on Darfur remain vital tools to curb the illicit flow of weapons that perpetuates this devastating conflict. For these measures to be effective, all Member States must strictly adhere to their obligations under resolution 1591 (2005) and refrain from any external interference, including the supply of weapons and the recruitment and financing of foreign fighters.

In this context, the independent, objective, and transparent monitoring carried out by the Panel of Experts is indispensable. We urge all parties and Member States to cooperate fully with the Panel to enable it to carry out its mandate effectively.

Finally, Greece reaffirms its unwavering commitment to the sovereignty, unity, independence, and territorial integrity of the Sudan, and reiterates its support for the mediation efforts led by the African Union and IGAD toward an inclusive and sustainable political solution.

I thank you.
after.Republic of Korea:
Thank you, Madam President.

The Republic of Korea welcomes the unanimous adoption of the resolution extending the mandate of the Panel of Experts assisting the 1591 Sudan Sanctions Committee for an additional year.

Speaking first in our capacity as the Chair of the 1591 Sanctions Committee, we express our sincere appreciation to all Council members for their constructive engagement and unity. The Panel of Experts plays an indispensable role in providing independent, factual, and timely reporting to assist the Committee in fulfilling its mandate. We urge all parties and Member States to cooperate fully with the Panel and ensure its unhindered access so that it may carry out its vital work objectively and effectively.

Now, allowing me to share a few remarks in my national capacity.

The Republic of Korea remains gravely alarmed by the relentless fighting and catastrophic humanitarian disaster in the Sudan, particularly in Darfur. The continued siege of El Fasher by the Rapid Support Forces, the indiscriminate shelling of civilian populated areas and displacement sites such as the Abu Shouk camp, and the alarming surge in conflict-related sexual violence are unacceptable and must cease immediately. All parties must strictly abide by their obligations under international humanitarian law and international human rights law.

We reiterate that compliance with the arms embargo is vital to curbing the violence. We call upon all Member States to strictly enforce the sanctions measures and to refrain from any external interference—including the illicit transfer of arms, materiel, and the recruitment of foreign fighters—that serves only to prolong the war and deepen the suffering of the Sudanese people.

Furthermore, full, safe, rapid, and unhindered humanitarian access across all borders and conflict lines is imperative to save lives and avert widespread famine. In this regard, we welcome the decision by the Sudanese authorities to keep the Adré border crossing open through the end of the year and encourage continued facilitation of cross-line and cross-border aid deliveries.

In conclusion, there can be no military solution to this conflict. We reaffirm our strong support for the sovereignty, unity, and territorial integrity of the Sudan, and once again urge the parties to commit to an immediate and permanent nationwide cessation of hostilities and engage in inclusive, peaceful political dialogue.

I thank you.
after.Russian Federation:
Madam President,

The Russian Federation voted in favour of the resolution extending the mandate of the Panel of Experts of the Security Council 1591 Committee on the Sudan for another twelve months.

Our position on the situation in the Sudan remains consistent and principled. We firmly support the sovereignty, independence, unity, and territorial integrity of the Sudan. We share the deep concern over the protracted armed conflict, which continues to cause immense hardship for the friendly Sudanese people, and we advocate for an immediate cessation of hostilities and the achievement of lasting peace through an inclusive national dialogue led by the Sudanese themselves, without external interference or imposed solutions.

In voting for the extension of the mandate of the Panel of Experts, we proceed from the understanding that its members will carry out their work strictly within the framework of their mandate, guided by the principles of objectivity, impartiality, and professionalism. The Panel’s findings and recommendations must be based on verified, credible, and corroborated facts, rather than unconfirmed reports or politicized narratives. Crucially, the Panel must conduct its work in close contact and constructive coordination with the legitimate authorities of the country—the Government of the Sudan.

We also reiterate our principled stance that Security Council sanctions cannot remain in place indefinitely, nor should they be used as an instrument of external political pressure. Restrictive measures imposed nearly two decades ago under completely different realities must be adapted to the current situation. In this regard, we emphasize the provision in the resolution concerning the review of benchmarks established under resolution 2676 (2023), and we expect that this review will be conducted in genuine partnership with the Sudanese authorities, with a view to the progressive lifting of these outdated restrictions. Council measures must not impede the ability of the Sudanese state to protect its civilians and maintain public order.

We also express grave concern over the continuing external interference in the conflict, including the illicit supply of arms and the recruitment, financing, and deployment of foreign mercenaries. Such actions only fuel further escalation and must be stopped immediately.

The Russian Federation will continue to provide support to the Sudan and its people, both bilaterally and within the Security Council, in the interests of restoring peace, security, and stability across the country.

Thank you.
after.Sierra Leone:
Madam President,

Sierra Leone voted in favour of the resolution just adopted, extending the mandate of the Panel of Experts assisting the 1591 Sanctions Committee for a period of twelve months. We thank the United States, as the penholder, for its efforts in facilitating negotiations that enabled Council unity today.

The renewal of the Panel’s mandate comes at a critical juncture. The ongoing conflict in the Sudan continues to inflict immense suffering on civilians, driving millions into acute food insecurity, famine conditions, and displacement. We remain deeply alarmed by the relentless fighting in Darfur, particularly the catastrophic siege and assault on El Fasher, as well as the repeated, deadly attacks on internally displaced persons in camps such as Abu Shouk. The alarming surge in conflict-related sexual and gender-based violence, grave violations against children, and attacks on medical and humanitarian personnel are intolerable.

For Sierra Leone, the harrowing scenes of violence and violations of international humanitarian law in the Sudan resonate deeply with our own history and our painful experience during our civil conflict. We know too well the devastating human toll of prolonged war, particularly on women and children. This is why we have consistently championed the protection of civilians and accountability as paramount imperatives for this Council.

In this context, the arms embargo on Darfur and the independent monitoring role of the Panel of Experts remain indispensable instruments. Destabilizing flows of weapons and ammunition, as well as the recruitment and deployment of foreign fighters and mercenaries, only serve to fuel and prolong the bloodshed. We urge all Member States to strictly comply with their obligations under the sanctions regime and to refrain from any external interference that undermines the peace and stability of the Sudan.

Madam President,

We welcome the sovereign decision of the Government of the Sudan to extend the opening of the Adre border crossing, which is vital for facilitating life-saving humanitarian assistance. We reiterate our call on all parties to respect international humanitarian law and guarantee rapid, safe, and unhindered humanitarian access to all civilians in need across the country.

At the same time, Sierra Leone reaffirms its unwavering commitment to the sovereignty, unity, independence, and territorial integrity of the Sudan. We underscore the importance of constructive engagement between the Panel of Experts and the Sudanese authorities, as well as the need for regular reviews of the benchmarks established under resolution 2676 (2023), with a view to adjusting measures as progress is achieved.

Ultimately, there is no military solution to this conflict. We call on the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces to immediately cease hostilities, de-escalate the fighting in Darfur and nationwide, and return to an inclusive, Sudanese-owned political dialogue facilitated by the African Union and IGAD. The resilient people of the Sudan have endured far too much; they deserve peace, justice, and the restoration of a stable, democratic future.

I thank you.
after.Slovenia:
Thank you, Madam President.

Slovenia welcomes the unanimous adoption of today’s resolution extending the mandate of the Panel of Experts assisting the 1591 Committee for another year, and we thank the United States for its leadership as penholder. Today, the Security Council has demonstrated much-needed unity in addressing the ongoing crisis in the Sudan.

The human catastrophe unfolding across the Sudan, and particularly in Darfur, remains deeply distressing. The continued escalation of violence, the brutal and relentless siege of El Fasher by the Rapid Support Forces, repeated attacks on civilians and displacement camps such as Abu Shouk, and the widespread destruction of critical infrastructure demand our unwavering focus. 

Slovenia remains particularly appalled by the alarming levels of conflict-related sexual violence, grave violations against children, and the denial of life-saving humanitarian assistance. We reiterate that all parties must strictly respect international humanitarian law and international human rights law. The protection of civilians, humanitarian workers, and medical personnel must be paramount. In this regard, we welcome the continued opening of the Adre border crossing and stress the imperative of sustained, safe, rapid, and unhindered cross-border and cross-line humanitarian access to all communities in need.

The arms embargo on Darfur is an essential tool to prevent further atrocities and de-escalate the conflict. We express grave concern over the continued influx of weapons and foreign fighters into Darfur, which only fuels the violence and deepens the suffering of the Sudanese people. We urge all Member States to fully comply with their obligations under the arms embargo and to refrain from any external interference.

To this end, the independent, impartial, and credible reporting of the Panel of Experts is more vital than ever. We call upon all parties and relevant stakeholders to extend their full cooperation to the Panel, granting them safe and unhindered access.

There is no military solution to this conflict. We call for an immediate cessation of hostilities, the lifting of the siege of El Fasher, and renewed commitment by all parties to an inclusive, peaceful political process that restores civilian rule and preserves the sovereignty, unity, and territorial integrity of the Sudan.

Thank you.
after.Somalia:
Madam President,

Somalia voted in favour of the resolution just adopted, which extends the mandate of the Panel of Experts assisting the 1591 Sudan Sanctions Committee for an additional year.

Our vote reflects our profound concern over the devastating conflict that continues to engulf our brotherly neighbour, the Sudan, and its severe humanitarian impact on millions of innocent civilians, particularly in Darfur and across the country. The ongoing military escalation, including the prolonged siege of El Fasher, attacks on internally displaced persons camps such as Abu Shouk, and the severe food insecurity facing the Sudanese people, require our urgent, collective, and coordinated attention.

Somalia reaffirms its unwavering commitment to the sovereignty, unity, independence, and territorial integrity of the Sudan. We firmly believe that the primary responsibility for protecting civilians and maintaining security lies with the Sudanese national authorities. In this context, sanctions regimes are not ends in themselves, but rather tools intended to support peace and stability. We welcome the inclusion of language emphasizing regular consultations and constructive engagement between the Panel of Experts and the Government of the Sudan, as well as the Council’s intention to review progress against established benchmarks with a view to considering the adjustment or progressive lifting of these measures.

Madam President,

The conflict in Sudan cannot be resolved militarily. It is imperative that all parties cease hostilities immediately, protect civilians and civilian infrastructure in accordance with international humanitarian law, and ensure safe, rapid, and unhindered humanitarian access. We also emphasize that external interference, including the illicit transfer of weapons and the recruitment and financing of foreign fighters, only exacerbates the violence and undermines prospects for peace. All Member States must respect and strictly enforce the existing arms embargo and refrain from actions that fuel the conflict.

Finally, Somalia reiterates its full support for regional and international diplomatic efforts, particularly those led by the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) and the African Union, to facilitate an inclusive, Sudanese-led, and Sudanese-owned political dialogue that restores peace, security, and institutional stability to the Sudan and the wider Horn of Africa region.

I thank you.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
Thank you, Madam President.

The United Kingdom welcomes the unanimous adoption of today’s resolution extending the mandate of the Panel of Experts assisting the 1591 Sudan Sanctions Committee for another year. We thank the United States, as penholder, for their leadership and constructive engagement in achieving this Council’s unity today.

The conflict in Sudan remains one of the world's worst humanitarian and protection crises. Over the past months, the situation in Darfur has grown ever more catastrophic. The Rapid Support Forces’ relentless assault and siege of El Fasher, as well as repeated attacks on civilian sites, healthcare facilities, and camps for internally displaced persons such as Abu Shouk, have caused unimaginable civilian death, destruction, and mass displacement, accompanied by horrific levels of sexual violence and acute famine.

In this context, the independent monitoring and reporting provided by the Panel of Experts is vital. Their work exposes the illicit flows of arms that fuel the conflict and documents gross violations of international humanitarian law and human rights abuses. Compliance with the targeted arms embargo on Darfur is an obligation on all Member States under Chapter VII of the UN Charter, and all parties must cease the illicit transfer of weapons and military material and halt external interference that prolongs this war.

We reiterate this Council's clear demand in resolution 2736 for the RSF to immediately halt the siege of El Fasher. All parties must de-escalate, protect civilians, uphold international humanitarian law, and ensure safe, rapid, and unhindered humanitarian access to all those in need. In this regard, we welcome the continued opening of the Adre border crossing and urge that all cross-border and cross-line routes remain accessible without impediment.

The people of Sudan have suffered for far too long. The United Kingdom remains steadfast in its support for the Sudanese people, for Sudan's sovereignty and territorial integrity, and for all regional and international efforts to achieve an immediate cessation of hostilities and a durable, inclusive peace.

Thank you.
